Define a CLI entrypoint that accepts exactly one positional argument, a string representing a non-negative integer N in decimal notation with no leading zeros except for '0'. Define a CLI entrypoint that accepts exactly one positional argument: a string representing a pattern for a simple Run-Length Encoded (RLE) list using only ASCII digits and lowercase Latin letters, with no whitespace. Each run in the string is required to be consecutive: a run consists of 1 to 3 ASCII digits (interpreted as a decimal integer in the inclusive range 1 to 255) followed by a single lowercase letter. At least one run must be present and no additional characters are allowed. On any invalid input (such as empty string, missing or extra digits, uppercase letters, digits out of range, or leftover characters), the CLI must print 'error' followed by a newline and exit with status 1. Define a CLI entrypoint that accepts exactly one positional argument: a string consisting solely of up to 50 ASCII lowercase letters ('a'-'z'). The CLI must print the shortest possible palindrome string that can be formed by inserting zero or more lowercase letters at the end of the input string. If the input string already forms a palindrome, print it unchanged. If the input is not composed entirely of 1 to 50 lowercase letters, print 'error' followed by a newline and exit with status 1. Otherwise, print the constructed palindrome (using only lowercase ASCII letters), followed by a single newline and exit with status 0. The output must always be deterministic; for non-palindromic input, the solution must add the minimal possible number of characters. Only letters may appear in output; preservation of input is required when already a palindrome. Edge cases: the empty string is not valid input; single-letter strings are valid and must print as-is. Deterministic failure: on invalid input, behavior must match error contract exactly. Output and code must be fully capturable in-process via sys.stdout and integer return code.
